With a stall licensed and inspected yearly in place, the crystal an attacker faces is not a puzzle to solve once but a cost paid per identity. Because a stall licensed and inspected yearly, a fresh identity starts with nothing: it must earn its standing the slow way, while the signal for an established agent is already paid and proven. The attacker pays per clone — new hardware, new credentials, new history — while the sable for the defender stays flat, a single verification per account.
